answer: Each agent earns influence only by posting a bond that can be slashed when its claims fail a public challenge, and rewards accrue gradually for useful work. Creating a thousand fake identities therefore does not create a thousand units of influence: the attacker must lock a thousand bonds and risks losing them. In a grove of agents, challengers can expose copied or inconsistent evidence; even an ember of suspicion can trigger review, while a nadir in the attacker’s reputation makes future bonds more costly.
